_comment: The journal crawl's cost bounds. THESE LIVE HERE, NOT IN CODE (Prompt 5).
Discovery is fetch-and-classify: every candidate link costs one request,
so these two numbers are the entire difference between crawling a journal
and crawling a publisher. Changing them must not need a recompile.
max_pages: hard budget per journal. A crawl that stops here has NOT
covered the journal, and the outcome says so — see StoppedBy::Budget.
Raised 40 -> 120 on 14 Sep 2026: at 40, nine of ten journals ended on
the budget with 48-464 candidates unvisited, and 40 had been chosen
before the crawl stopped wandering into research articles and sibling
journals. Which journals still end on the budget at 120 is the number
that says whether the bound or the domain is the limit.
max_depth: 0 is the entry page alone; 3 is §3.4's stated bound.
author_services_hosts: publisher-wide guideline domains, which are not the
journal's own host but do carry its requirements. Allowlisted, never
inferred, because 'the publisher's domain' is not something a crawler can
derive from a URL without wandering.
MEASURED vs UNMEASURED — the distinction this list now carries, because
one entry was removed on evidence and the rest have never been looked at.
REMOVED, measured: authorservices.springernature.com. Across Nature
Medicine's crawl it contributed 9 requirements, ALL NINE FALSE (paid
translation turnaround times and pricing tiers stored as word limits),
and 8 of the 11 pages that were admitted as guidance and were not
guidance at all — a storefront root, four service sales pages and three
marketing blog posts. 0/9 precision. See §11 D163.
UNMEASURED, still listed: authorservices.wiley.com,
authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com, www.elsevier.com, journals.plos.org,
www.biomedcentral.com. NOBODY HAS RUN THE MEASUREMENT ON THESE. They are
not 'checked and kept'; they are 'never looked at'. Wiley's and T&F's
author-services sites may well be genuinely instructional where Springer
Nature's is a shop — one publisher's result does not transfer.
HOW TO CHECK ONE before trusting or dropping it, per publisher:
cargo run --example journal_barren_probe -- <journal entry url>
-> reads every admitted page that yielded no requirement, so each can
be classified by hand as extractor gap / gate error / correctly
barren. The host's pages appear with their titles and headings.
cargo run --example journal_extract_probe -- <journal entry url>
-> every extracted requirement WITH ITS SPAN and source URL, which is
what makes a price list distinguishable from a word limit.
The number that decides it is the host's requirement precision. At 0/N
the unit is the host, not the path (D163).
profiled_journals: the ten §3.4 names, as (key, display name, crawl entry),
then twenty Elsevier journals (§11 D252): key = the ScienceDirect slug,
entry = sciencedirect.com/journal/<slug>/publish/guide-for-authors.
MOVED HERE from a const in examples/journal_crawl_probe.rs, which is an
example binary the app cannot read — so the picker had no way to offer
'the ten profiled journals' that the architecture document describes.
The `key` is the primary key of every journal_* table and of the
fingerprint's provenance row; changing one orphans that journal's rows.
journal_path_segments: how many leading path segments identify the JOURNAL
on a host that serves many. journals.plos.org/plosone/... is one;
frontiersin.org/journals/public-health/... is two; a host that serves one
journal is absent from this map and scopes to the whole host.
Measured: without it, a crawl of PLOS ONE wandered into PLOS Genetics,
PLOS Pathogens and PLOS Biology and spent one journal's budget on six;
and a crawl of The Lancet reached six sibling Lancet journals' homepages.
IT DOES NOT FIT EVERY PUBLISHER, and that is a limit of the approach
rather than a missing entry. Wiley identifies a journal by an id that
appears at varying path positions (/page/journal/10970258/... and
/journal/10970258/...), so no leading-segment prefix isolates it; SAGE's
entry path (/author-instructions/JHP) names the SECTION first and the
journal second. Both are left absent, which scopes them to the whole
host and shows up as off-journal pages in the crawl list — visible,
which is the property that makes this rule acceptable at all.
identity_path_segments: which journal OWNS a URL, where that differs from
how far its crawl may go. Read by key_for_url before
journal_path_segments, never by the crawl. 0 = the host is one journal.
A host in NEITHER map claims nothing (§11 D226): an absent host used to
mean the host is the journal, which bound every Wiley and SAGE journal's
guidelines page to Statistics in Medicine or J Health Psychology. Wiley
3 is page/journal/<id>, the entry's form; a /journal/<id>/ URL does not
match it and claims nothing, which is the safe way to be incomplete.
corpus_bounds: the comparable corpus's size. Below `minimum` a convention
is UNAVAILABLE however good the data looks — an inference from six
papers is not an inference. `target` is what a build aims for and
`maximum` caps the fetch. Prompt 5 requires all three in config.
